question.text: Does septoplasty change the dimensions of compensatory hypertrophy of the middle turbinate?
question.context: To measure the dimensions of compensatory hypertrophy of the middle turbinate in patients with nasal septal deviation, before and after septoplasty. The mucosal and bony structures of the middle turbinate and the angle of the septum were measured using radiological analysis before septoplasty and at least one year after septoplasty. All pre- and post-operative measurements of the middle turbinate were compared using the paired sample t-test and Wilcoxon rank sum test. The dimensions of bony and mucosal components of the middle turbinate on concave and convex sides of the septum were not significantly changed by septoplasty. There was a significant negative correlation after septoplasty between the angle of the septum and the middle turbinate total area on the deviated side (p = 0.033).

medgemma_4b.critical_evidence: There was no significant change in the dimensions of bony and mucosal components of the middle turbinate on concave and convex sides of the septum after septoplasty.
medgemma_4b.differential_considered: While the study didn't directly address compensatory hypertrophy, the lack of change in the middle turbinate dimensions after septoplasty makes it unlikely that septoplasty would significantly alter the compensatory hypertrophy. Other nasal issues could potentially affect the middle turbinate, but the study's findings don't support that.
